newsitem.title: USA: Mistrial for white cops charged in death of black.
newsitem.headline: Mistrial for white cops charged in death of black.

text.p: A judge declared a mistrial Friday in the racially charged case of two white policemen accused of the suffocation death of a black motorist.
Allegheny County Judge David Cashman declined to give specifics about his decision and has imposed a gag order on all court participants. A mistrial does not preclude a trial at a later date.

Brentwood Lt. Milton Mulholland, 57, and Baldwin Patrolman Michael Albert, 32, were charged with one count each of involuntary manslaughter in the Oct. 12, 1995, suffocation death of Jonny Gammage, 31, a cousin and business partner of Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Ray Seals.
Brentwood and Baldwin are Pittsburgh suburbs. Gammage died on a roadside in another suburb, Overbrook, after he was pulled over by Mulholland.

Patrick Thomassey, defence attorney for the policemen, had requested a mistrial late Thursday after several verbal jousts with Allegheny County Coroner Cyril Wecht, who was hired by the Gammage family to review the case. Wecht testified that Gammage had died of asphyxiation "after he was compressed in a prone position on the pavement."

The officers testified in a coroner's inquest that Gammage was driving erratically and became violent when he got out of his car. They said they were forced to restrain him by holding him on the ground.

The trial, before an all-white jury consisting of nine women and three men, had raised racial tensions here and had been compared with the 1991 beating of black motorist Rodney King by four white police officers whose acquittal sparked major rioting in Los Angeles.
